questions.q: How was time measured through history, and how does a pendulum help?
answer: Time has always been measured by using events that repeat regularly.

answer.text: People first used natural repeating events such as day and night, the phases of the Moon and the seasons. Later they built devices like the sundial, the water clock and the sand clock or hourglass.

Galileo noticed that a simple pendulum — a bob hung by a thread — swings to and fro with a steady rhythm. One complete to-and-fro swing is an oscillation, and the time for one oscillation, the time period, is constant for a given pendulum. This steady time period made pendulum clocks possible.
Modern clocks use quartz for great accuracy, and the SI unit of time is the second.

questions.q: Define speed, and explain how a distance–time graph shows different kinds of motion.

answer.text: Speed is the distance travelled in a unit of time, found by dividing distance by time. Its SI unit is the metre per second, though vehicle speeds are often given in kilometres per hour. A speedometer shows a vehicle's speed and an odometer the distance travelled.

In such a graph, time is plotted on the horizontal axis and distance on the vertical axis. A straight sloping line shows uniform motion, in which equal distances are covered in equal times. A horizontal line shows that the object is at rest, since its distance does not change. A curved line shows non-uniform motion, and the steeper the line, the greater the speed.

questions.q: What is a simple pendulum, and what are the terms oscillation and time period?

answer.text: A simple pendulum is a small heavy ball, called the bob, hung from a fixed point by a thread. When the bob is pulled to one side and released, it swings to and fro about its central resting position.
One complete to-and-fro movement of the bob, from one end to the other and back again, is called one oscillation. The pendulum keeps oscillating for some time before coming to rest.

The time taken by the pendulum to complete one oscillation is called its time period. A remarkable fact is that the time period of a given pendulum stays the same for each swing. Because of this regularity, the pendulum was used to make accurate clocks.

answer: Thus a simple pendulum swings to and fro, one full swing being an oscillation, and the time for one oscillation is its time period, which stays constant.

questions.q: Distinguish between uniform and non-uniform motion.
answer: When an object moves, its motion may be uniform or non-uniform, depending on its speed.

answer.text: In uniform motion, an object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, so its speed stays the same throughout. For example, a train moving steadily at the same speed on a straight track is in uniform motion. On a distance-time graph, uniform motion is shown by a straight sloping line.

In non-uniform motion, an object covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time, so its speed keeps changing. A bus moving through crowded traffic, speeding up and slowing down, shows non-uniform motion. On a distance-time graph, it is shown by a curved line.

answer: Thus in uniform motion the speed is constant, while in non-uniform motion the speed keeps changing.
